newsitem.title: GERMANY: Data shows German economy a bit stronger.
newsitem.headline: Data shows German economy a bit stronger.

text.p: Data released by the central bank Wednesday showed that the German economy was slightly stronger in the fourth quarter than previously believed, although economists said the picture was still not one of a vigorous recovery.

The statistics released by the Bundesbank showed a rise of 0.1 percent in gross domestic product in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the previous quarter and of 2.2 percent from a year earlier. The rates were calculated by Reuters from the raw data.
Figures two weeks ago had shown a 0.2 percent decline from the previous quarter and 1.6 percent year-on-year rise.
The main strength of the Bundesbank data was derived from downward revisions to earlier figures.
"These data show the economy was not as weak as we thought. At least now it's not a fall but a marginal rise," said economist Holger Fahrinkrug at UBS in Frankfurt.
"Still, even these numbers are highly uncertain. Seasonal adjustments are putting a bias on the data. The 2.2 percent in particular looks excessively strong," Fahrinkrug said.
Federal Statistics Office data Wednesday put the fourth-quarter year-on-year rise at only 1.9 percent.

Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said the flat fourth quarter was not a sign of a renewed period of economic weakness and the government stood by its forecast of 2.5 percent economic growth this year.
Most private-sector economists predict lower growth of about 2.0 percent.
